Imperfect detection of a community

Source: R/detection.R
observe_detection.Rd

Turns the true abundances of a simulation into what a survey would record. Each individual is detected in each of visits visits with probability detection, independently, so the count of a species at a site in a visit is binomial and a species with more individuals is more likely to be found, as in the models of Royle & Nichols (2003) and Royle (2004). The record keeps the largest count over visits, or only whether the species was detected. The same applies to every step of series, with new visits at each step. Use it inside simulate in abc_table(), with detection drawn from a prior, so that the reference table carries the same observation error as the data.

Usage

observe_detection(x, detection, visits = 3, record = c("counts", "presence"))

Arguments

x

An mc_sim object or an mc_data() object with true abundances.

detection

Probability that an individual is detected in a visit: one number, or one per species, named by species.

visits

Number of visits to each site.

record

"counts" for the largest count over visits or "presence" for detected at least once (1) or not (0).

Value

An mc_data() object with the recorded comm and series, and the attribute detection.

References

Royle, J. A., & Nichols, J. D. (2003). Estimating abundance from repeated presence–absence data or point counts. Ecology, 84, 777–790. doi:10.1890/0012-9658(2003)084[0777:EAFRPA]2.0.CO;2

Royle, J. A. (2004). N-mixture models for estimating population size from spatially replicated counts. Biometrics, 60, 108–115. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2004.00142.x

See also

Other inference: abc_choose(), abc_cv(), abc_diagnose(), abc_fit(), abc_ppc(), abc_recovery(), abc_table(), fold_summarise(), spatial_folds()

Examples

tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(8)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(landscape_grid(side = 4), species_traits(tree, 0.5),
                              competition_matrix(tree, "none"), dispersal = 0.05,
                              n_steps = 40)
seen <- observe_detection(sim, detection = 0.1, visits = 3)
c(true = sum(sim$abundance > 0), recorded = sum(seen$comm > 0))
#>     true recorded 
#>       91       66
